title: The Asteroid That Hit Earth—And No One Noticed for 10 Years
hook: A 100-meter asteroid struck the ocean in 2017, and NASA only found out years later because of military satellite data.
why_this_can_go_viral: It exploits the fear of an invisible catastrophe and the shock that authorities missed it.

title: The Star That Emits a Signal That Matches Human DNA
hook: A star 400 light-years away pulses at a frequency that mirrors the electromagnetic signature of DNA—and it’s been doing it for billions of years.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea that the universe might be broadcasting the blueprint of life is profound and deeply curiosity-driven.

title: The Black Hole That Flipped Its Magnetic Field—And Aimed at Earth
hook: A supermassive black hole suddenly reversed its magnetic poles, and now its jet points directly at our solar system.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines the terror of a black hole with the twist that it just turned to face us—a ticking time bomb.

title: The Classified Mission That Found a City Beneath the Moon's Surface
hook: Declassified military documents reveal an Apollo-era mission detected a massive hollow structure 50 miles below the lunar surface.
why_this_can_go_viral: Taps into the enduring conspiracy theory that the Moon hides alien structures, backed by 'declassified' docs.

title: The Extinction Event That Turned the Ocean into Acid in 24 Hours
hook: 252 million years ago, the ocean pH dropped so fast that 96% of marine life died within a single day.
why_this_can_go_viral: The shocking speed of the event makes it feel relevant to today's climate fears—immediate and terrifying.

title: The Dark Matter That Created a 'Knot' in Space-Time Over Earth
hook: Satellites detected a gravitational anomaly above the Atlantic—a knot of dark matter that bends light around it.
why_this_can_go_viral: Visualizing dark matter as a physical 'knot' in space is eerie and makes the abstract feel tangible.

title: The Fermi Paradox Answer: The Universe Is a Graveyard
hook: A new statistical model suggests that civilizations don't go silent—they all die before they can leave their star system.
why_this_can_go_viral: Offers a bleak, definitive answer to one of humanity's biggest questions—drives existential dread.

title: The Signal That Came from a Star That Hadn't Formed Yet
hook: Astronomers detected a repeating radio burst from a region of empty space—only to realize the star that sent it won't exist for 50 million years.
why_this_can_go_viral: Challenges causality and time—makes viewers question if signals can travel backward through time.

title: The Asteroid That Broke in Half—And Both Halves Kept Flying at Earth
hook: In 2023, an asteroid split into two equal chunks—and both pieces corrected their course to still hit Earth's atmosphere.
why_this_can_go_viral: Implies an almost intelligent behavior—feels like a scene from a sci-fi horror film.

title: The Declassified Map That Shows a 'Planet X' Orbit Inside the Oort Cloud
hook: A 1970s military astronomer's map, recently declassified, plots a massive object with an orbit that brings it inside the Solar System every 800 years.
why_this_can_go_viral: Nibiru theories have massive viral traction—this feels like the smoking gun document.

title: The Star That Spews a Particle Beam That Rotates Through Earth Every 1,000 Years
hook: A neutron star's beam sweeps across Earth's orbital path—and based on its precession, the next hit is due in 80 years.
why_this_can_go_viral: Gives a specific deadline—viewers love countdowns to cosmic disasters.

title: The Mass Extinction That Wiped Out All Insects—And Left a Silent World
hook: 250 million years ago, an extinction event killed every insect on Earth. The silence lasted for 5 million years.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea of a world without insects is deeply unsettling—everyone knows how important they are.

title: The Dark Matter That Causes 'Ghost Gravity' in Empty Space
hook: Galaxies are moving as if pulled by something massive—in regions where there is absolutely nothing. Dark matter is creating gravity from voids.
why_this_can_go_viral: Inverts expectation—dark matter isn't just in galaxies, it haunts the empty void.

title: The Fermi Paradox Answer: They're All in Hiding from the Same Thing
hook: A mathematical analysis suggests that if one civilization becomes a predator, all others must hide. The universe is silent because it's terrified.
why_this_can_go_viral: Based on the popular 'Dark Forest' theory—highly shareable, deeply paranoid, and feels like a horror movie.

title: The Galaxy That Emits a 'Hum' at the Exact Frequency of Human Consciousness
hook: A distant galaxy radiates a continuous low-frequency hum—measured at 40 Hz, the same frequency as human gamma brainwaves.
why_this_can_go_viral: Connects the cosmic with the personal—viewers feel a direct link between their own mind and the universe.

title: The Rogue Planet That Carries an Ocean of Liquid Nitrogen—Aimed at Earth
hook: A planet-sized object with a -200°C ocean is on a trajectory that will pass through the inner Solar System, dragging a trail of frozen death.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines the rogue planet trope with a specific, weirdly terrifying composition—ice as a weapon.

title: The Classified CIA Report That Describes a 'Gravity Lens' Over the Pacific
hook: A 1972 CIA memo describes a sensor anomaly that behaved like a gravitational lens—over the ocean, not in space.
why_this_can_go_viral: Makes the viewer feel like the government has known about weird gravity events for decades.

title: The Extinction Event That Was Caused by a 'Star Eating Its Own Planet'
hook: A nearby star swallowed a gas giant—the resulting energy pulse sterilized half the galaxy's life forms 600 million years ago.
why_this_can_go_viral: A novel extinction mechanism—most people don't think of stars eating planets as a threat.

title: The Dark Matter Particle That Turns Into Light When It Hits Earth's Core
hook: Physicists believe a specific dark matter particle reaches Earth's iron core and annihilates—producing a flash of gamma rays from the center of the planet.
why_this_can_go_viral: Imagining the Earth's core as a dark matter reactor is both cool and unsettling.

title: The Signal That Arrived from a Star That Exploded 2,000 Years Ago—Perfectly Timed
hook: A supernova's neutrino burst arrived at Earth exactly on the anniversary of a historical event—as if the universe was sending a message.
why_this_can_go_viral: Blends astronomy with numerology—viewers love patterns that feel deliberate.

title: The Black Hole That Threw a Planet Out of Its Galaxy at 30% Light Speed
hook: A planet was slingshotted by a black hole at 90,000 km/s—it's now a rogue world traveling through intergalactic space.
why_this_can_go_viral: A planet moving at relativistic speeds is mind-blowing—like a cosmic bullet.

title: The Declassified Space Shuttle Mission That Carried a Weapon—Into Orbit
hook: A 1985 Space Shuttle mission secretly deployed a prototype missile platform that could target satellites—and it was never retrieved.
why_this_can_go_viral: Reveals that the US tested weapons in space decades ago—feels like a hidden history lesson.

title: The Star That Dims by 80% Every 72 Years—And Nobody Knows Why
hook: A red giant in the constellation Cygnus fades dramatically every 72 years, as if something massive is passing in front of it—something invisible.
why_this_can_go_viral: A regular, unexplained dimming cycle feels like a cosmic clock—drives pattern-seeking obsession.

title: The Rogue Black Hole That Carries a 'Dead Galaxy' Inside Its Event Horizon
hook: A black hole ejected from its galaxy still contains the compressed matter of an entire star system—it's a tomb flying through the void.
why_this_can_go_viral: Poetic and dark—a dead galaxy entombed in a black hole is a haunting image.

title: The Comet That Carries a Molecule That Replaces Oxygen in Blood—And Kills Instantly
hook: A comet contains a cyanide compound that binds to hemoglobin 100x faster than oxygen—a single breath of its dust would cause instant death.
why_this_can_go_viral: Personalizes cosmic danger—it's not just an impact, it's a chemical weapon from space.
